captions.text: 1920: the Soviet republics stand as one bloc.
1920: Nauru passes from the war occupation to the mandate: Australian troops 'held control until 1920' (History of Nauru); 'the terms of the League of Nations mandate were drawn up in 1920' (Nauru).
1920 (page silent on the date): Greek forces leave the south.
1920 (page silent on the date): French forces leave Korçë and Shkodër.
1920 (page silent on the date): Serbian troops leave the northern mountains.
1920: the Saudis take Abha and the highlands.
1920: the Tashkent countryside is lost to the Reds.
1920: the Nugaal Valley passes back.
1920: the League of Nations takes over the Micronesian islands for Japan.
1920: the South Seas Mandate.
1920: Japan occupies northern Sakhalin.
Summer 1920: Greek offensives extend the zone to Bursa and Usak.
1920: Batum is incorporated.
1920: the Australian military control of Nauru ends: Australian troops 'held control until 1920' (History of Nauru); the mandate itself is dated 1923 on the pages (terms drawn up in 1920).

1920: Nauru passes to the Australian mandate: 'The terms of the League of Nations mandate were drawn up in 1920' (Nauru), conferred on Australia in 1923 with the United Kingdom and New Zealand as co-trustees (History of Nauru).
Early 1920: 'In early 1920, Romanian troops departed Hungary.'
1920: Eupen and Malmedy pass to Belgium.
1920: Italy leaves Albania's Bay of Vlore.
1920: Lithuania secures Vilnius from the Bolsheviks.
Early 1920: 'In early 1920, Romanian troops departed Hungary.'
1920 (Cliopatria's year): the Treaty of Sèvres (1920) would give Greece 'Smyrna and its surroundings and likely Constantinople and Thrace'; the page does not date the Greek occupation of Thrace.
1920s: the Cabinda protectorate is incorporated into the colony.
1920s: effective occupation is completed.
1920: the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic takes the Emirate of Bukhara's land.
1920: the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic takes the Khanate of Khiva's land.
1920: the last Whites hold Crimea.
Autumn 1920: Zeligowski's mutiny creates Central Lithuania under Polish protection.
Autumn 1920: the Vilnius dispute with Lithuania.
1920: South West Africa becomes a League of Nations mandate under South Africa.

1920: South Africa holds South West Africa as a Class C mandate, 'administered as 5th province of the Union' (Union page); Walvis Bay was administered with it from 1922 under the South West Africa Affairs Act (Walvis Bay page).
1920: the name Tanganyika takes effect.
1920: the Saudis take Abha and the Asir highlands.
1920: the Tashkent countryside returns to the republic.

1920: Northern Schleswig goes to Denmark after plebiscites held in February and March 1920 (Versailles page); the transfer date is not on the page, and Cliopatria's 1920 shape still holds it. [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart 'denmark' (dossier starts 1945) changed to kingdom-of-denmark-181
1920, 16 January: "Grigory Semyonov announced in Chita the creation of the 'Government of the Russian Eastern Outskirts'" (infobox "Established: January 16 1920").
10 January 1920: the Saar Basin Territory is created under a League of Nations Governing Commission.
January 1920: the Congress of Lushnjë makes Tirana the capital.
1920, 3 January: the ceasefire takes effect ('the peace treaty was concluded on 31 December 1919 and the ceasefire took effect on 3 January 1920'); the Treaty of Tartu follows on 2 February 1920.
January 1920: the French fight the Turkish national forces in Cilicia.
1920, 7 January: "The pursuing Red 5th Army took Tomsk on 20 December 1919 ...

1920, 20 January: "On 20 January the government in Irkutsk surrendered power to a Bolshevik military committee" (the Political Centre had formed in late December 1919); the Red Army "did not enter Irkutsk until 7 March".
1920, 3-10 January: the Red Southern Front takes Taganrog, Novocherkassk, Rostov-on-Don and Tikhoretsk.

1920, January: the Southern Front "pushed the Armed Forces of South Russia back to the Black Sea and North Caucasus by early 1920" (Rostov-Novocherkassk operation, 3-10 January); the page does not date Tsaritsyn (Volgograd) or the rest of the Don.

1920, 4 January: Kolchak's last decree transfers supreme power to Denikin and gives Semyonov "full military and civilian authority" in the Eastern Fringe; the buffer east of Baikal becomes Semyonov's own.
1920, 7 January: "The pursuing Red 5th Army took Tomsk on 20 December 1919 ...
1920, 4 January: the Russian State ends with Kolchak's last decree; Kolchak was shot at Irkutsk on 6 or 7 February 1920, the Alexander Kolchak page giving both dates.

Under the 1920 Accord of al-Rajma Idris was 'permitted to administer autonomously the oases around Kufra'; Kufra was 'the last stronghold of the Senussi in Libya' until 'In 1931, Italian forces seized Kufra'.
1920, 3-10 January: the Red Southern Front takes Taganrog, Novocherkassk, Rostov-on-Don and Tikhoretsk and reaches the Sea of Azov (Rostov-Novocherkassk operation; day and month only on the page).

1920, January: the Southern Front "pushed the Armed Forces of South Russia back to the Black Sea and North Caucasus by early 1920" (the Rostov-Novocherkassk operation, 3-10 January; the front was renamed the South-Western Front on 10 January 1920).
1920: Posen and Pomerelia pass to Poland.
1920: the Saar Basin passes to League of Nations control 'for 15 years' after which a plebiscite would decide sovereignty; the start date is not on the page (treaty in force 10 January 1920).
1920: Danzig and its hinterland are ceded for the League to establish the Free City of Danzig; the page gives no date (treaty in force 10 January 1920).
1920: Memel is 'ceded to the Allied and Associated powers for disposal'; the Territorial evolution page adds it was later transferred to Lithuania 'without a vote'.
1920: the Khan of Khiva abdicates and the Khorezm republic is born.
15 February 1920: France takes over the Memel Territory.

February 1920: the British retake the Dervish headquarters and the interior of British Somaliland (mirror of dervish-state ledger 7). Dervish state page, opened 2026-11-01: 'The town of Taleh was mostly destroyed after a RAF aerial bombardment in early February 1920'; 'Within a month, the British had occupied the capital of the Dervish State'.
February 1920: the British take Taleh.
February 1920: the Dervish state ends at Taleh.
1920, 2 February: the Treaty of Tartu fixes the border.
29 February 1920: the monarchy is restored without a king.
2 February 1920: the last khan abdicates and the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic follows.
15 February 1920: French troops and High Commissioner Dominique Odry administer the territory for the Allied powers.
1920: Latgale cleared of Soviet forces.
1920, winter: the rest of Ukraine falls to the Reds: "by 1920 all of Eastern and central Ukraine except Crimea was again in Bolshevik hands" (Ukrainian War of Independence page).
1920: the Bolsheviks retake Transcaspia.
1920: the Tashkent Soviet regains Transcaspia.
1920, winter: "by 1920 all of Eastern and central Ukraine except Crimea was again in Bolshevik hands" (Ukrainian War of Independence page).
8 March 1920: the Emirate is proclaimed a kingdom with Faisal I as king and Hashim al-Atassi as prime minister.
1920, 26-27 March: the Volunteer Army is evacuated from Novorossiysk; on 18-20 April the Kuban Army surrenders to the Red Army and the Kuban and North Caucasus are Soviet.
1920, 26-27 March: the Volunteer Army's remaining troops are evacuated from Novorossiysk to the Crimea.
1920, late March: the Southern Front ends on the mainland with the evacuation from Novorossiysk; only the Kuban Army (to April) and the Crimea remain.
1920, 28 April: "The Azerbaijan SSR was established on 28 April 1920 after the surrender of the government of the" Azerbaijan Democratic Republic.

1920, 6 April: a hastily convened Constituent Assembly at Verkhneudinsk proclaims the Far Eastern Republic, a buffer state between Soviet Russia and Japan; at first it comprises "only the area around Verkhneudinsk".
1920: the Allies give France the mandate for Syria and Lebanon.
28 April 1920: the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic ceases to exist when the Soviet 11th Army occupies it; the Armenian claim passes to Soviet Azerbaijan.
28 April 1920: the republic ceases to exist, ending its contest with Armenia over Karabakh, Zangezur and Nakhichevan.
1920: page silent on the Mughan Soviet Republic's end; the dossier closes the contest at the republic's own end, 28 April 1920, as a bridging judgment.
April-May 1920: the Soviet 11th Army 'conquered Karabakh in May 1920'; Nakhichevan 'was Sovietized later in 1920'.
28 April 1920: the Soviet 11th Army occupies the republic and it 'ceased to exist'.
1920: the owner's label changes; the occupation does not end.
1920: the Japanese occupation of the Maritime Provinces continues against the Far Eastern Republic, whose territory included 'the Maritime Province' (page).
April 1920: the mandate holds the French-occupied Cilician belt.
1920, 28 April: Soviet Azerbaijan is established.

1920, 4 April: the Government of South Russia is established (infobox "Established: 4 April 1920") in Sevastopol, successor to Denikin's South Russian Government ("set up in February 1920"); it adopted the name "Government of South Russia" officially on 16 August 1920 and France recognised it in August 1920.
1920, April: the capital moves to Sevastopol (infobox of the Government of South Russia); the South Russia page says Wrangel "set up a new government in Sevastopol ...
1920, 18-20 April: the Kuban Army, which replaced the Caucasus Army on 29 January 1920, surrenders to the Red Army; the Kuban and the North Caucasus are lost.
1920, 25 April: "The Kiev Expedition, in which 65,000 Polish and 15,000 Ukrainian soldiers took part, commenced on 25 April 1920"; Zhytomyr was captured on 26 April, Kiev entered on 7 May.
1920, 26 April: "Zhytomyr was captured on 26 April" by the Polish-Ukrainian forces.
April 1920: the military occupation of Palestine gives way to the mandate (next event).
25 April 1920: France receives the mandate for Syria and Lebanon.
April 1920: the coast of Lebanon passes from military occupation to the mandate (25 April 1920, the grant; Greater Lebanon proclaimed 1 September 1920).
25 April 1920: Britain is assigned the mandate for Palestine.
1920: the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic is proclaimed at Rasht.

1920: Gilan passes from the Qajar government to the republic of Mirza Kuchik Khan, supported by the Soviet Caspian Fleet that entered Anzali in May 1920 while the British garrison 'evacuated the town without any resistance'.
1920: Soviet ships enter Anzali.
1920: Mirza Kuchik Khan's Jangali partisans set up the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic in Gilan with Red Army help, capital Rasht.
7 May 1920: Poland and its Ukrainian allies take Kyiv.
1920, 7 May: "The combined Polish-Ukrainian forces under General Rydz-Smigly entered the city on 7 May."
4 June 1920: Trianon gives Transylvania and central Banat to Romania ('Romania gained all of Transylvania'; 'the whole of Transylvania was taken by Romania' on the Kingdom page).
4 June 1920: Trianon gives the south to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes: 'Croatia-Slavonia, Medjimurje, Banat, Backa and Baranja, and two-thirds of the Slovene March (Prekmurje)'.
4 June 1920: Trianon confirms Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia for Czechoslovakia.

4 June 1920: the Treaty of Trianon, signed 'on 4 June 1920' and in force 26 July 1921, gives Romania 'all of Transylvania, which was home to 2,800,000 Romanians'; 'The central parts of Banat were later assigned to Romania' (Crisana and Maramures are not named on the page, so the region is the researcher's reading).
June 1920: the Soviet counter-offensive.

1920, June: "In June 1920, Wrangel launched his last major offensive, the Northern Taurida Operation" and "his forces broke out of the Crimean bottleneck and captured a large territory to the north" (Pyotr Wrangel page).

1920, June: the Soviet counteroffensive (28 May; the 1st Cavalry Army broke through on 5 June and reached Zhytomyr and Berdychiv by 7 June) forces the Poles out: "After 10 June, Rydz-Smigly evacuated the 3rd Polish Army from Kiev.

1920, June: "In June 1920, Wrangel launched his last major offensive, the Northern Taurida Operation" and "his forces broke out of the Crimean bottleneck and captured a large territory to the north" (Pyotr Wrangel page; the page names no towns).
4 June 1920: Trianon confirms the north and east.
July 1920: a British civilian administration under a High Commissioner takes over Palestine.
1920: the Zhili clique wins the capital.
14 July 1920: the Zhili-Anhui War begins ('July 14, 1920 - July 23, 1920'); the page names Zhuozhou, Gaobei, Beicang, Langfang and Nanyuan.
23 July 1920: the Anhui clique is beaten.
1920 (bridging): the Anhui expedition's hold on Mongolia ends with the clique's defeat; the pages opened date neither the withdrawal nor the Soviet and Ungern events of 1921.
1920, 31 July: the republic is re-established in Minsk (the page gives the date, not the military operation).
1920, 28 July: the Spa Conference divides Cieszyn Silesia.
1920, 28 July: Czechoslovakia receives 58.1% of Cieszyn Silesia (the western and southern part, including the area east of the Olza that the page calls Trans-Olza), by decision of the Spa Conference.
1920, summer: the Soviet government of the Amur territory agrees to join; on 15 July 1920 Japan agrees in a truce with the Red Army to recognise the new buffer state.
10 July 1920: North Schleswig returns to Denmark.
1920, 31 July: Soviet Byelorussia is established.
28 July 1920: the Spa Conference divides Cieszyn Silesia.
28 July 1920: Czechoslovakia receives the larger part of Cieszyn Silesia.
1920, 26 August: the Kirghiz ASSR is established as "an autonomous republic within the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic", on the steppe north of the Turkestan ASSR.
1920: the Alash Autonomy is dissolved.
28 August 1920: the Red Army attacks Bukhara.
10 August 1920: the Treaty of Sevres gives Greece Eastern Thrace.
1920, 26 August: the Kirghiz ASSR is established as "an autonomous republic within the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic".
1920: Chen Jiongming invades Guangdong.
1920: the Latvian-Soviet Riga Peace Treaty is signed on 11 August 1920, ending the war (talks began 16 April 1920).
1920, 26 August: the Kirghiz ASSR is formed inside the RSFSR (renamed Kazak ASSR on 19 April 1925); it is a union republic from 3 December 1936.
September 1920: Italy leaves Albania except Sazan.
28 September 1920: the Turkish army under Karabekir invades Armenia.
2 September 1920: 'after four days of fighting, the emir's citadel (the Ark) was destroyed.'
2 September 1920: the Emirate falls.
1920: the Treaty of Seeb ends the rebellion.
25 September 1920: the Treaty of Seeb ends the rebellion; it 'resulted in a de facto split between Oman and Muscat'.
25 September 1920: the Imamate accepts the Sultan's sovereignty with autonomy.
25 September 1920: the interior becomes autonomous under the Imamate.
1920: the republic becomes the Turkestan Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic.
1920: Eupen-Malmedy to Belgium.
1920: the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic is proclaimed.
12 October 1920: Żeligowski proclaims the Republic of Central Lithuania at Vilnius.
30 October 1920: in the invasion begun on 28 September the Turkish army under Karabekir occupies the city of Kars, 'supposed to be impregnable', leaving its 25,000 defenders disorganised (page).
12 October 1920: the new state is a puppet of Poland from its founding.
10 October 1920: the Ikhwan attack Kuwait at Jahra.
10 October 1920: the Carinthian plebiscite keeps the south-east in Austria.
1920, 14 October: the Treaty of Tartu gives Finland Petsamo.

1920, 14 October: the Treaty of Tartu "was signed on 14 October 1920" (in force 31 December 1920) and "Finland additionally received Petsamo, with its ice-free harbour on the Arctic Ocean"; the page gives no date for the transfer itself.

1920, 28 October: the Red Southern Front advances out of the Kakhovka bridgehead into Northern Taurida (Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol, Chongar, 28 October to 3 November), then through Perekop and Chongar (7-17 November).
10 October 1920: the Carinthian plebiscite keeps the south-east in Austria.

1920, 29 November: "Soviet Armenia was established on 29 November 1920, with the Sovietisation of the short-lived First Republic of Armenia"; on 2 December Yerevan signed a pact with Moscow "securing Armenian statehood as a Soviet republic".
15 November 1920: the Free City of Danzig is established.
November 1920: Zangezur 'ceded by Azerbaijan to Armenia' as a 'symbol of friendship'; the war ends (infobox 28 November 1920).
7 November 1920: Żeligowski's army advances beyond Vilnius.
21 November 1920: the ceasefire takes effect.
Autumn 1920: Poland takes the Vilnius area.
Autumn 1920: Vilnius passes to Zeligowski's Central Lithuania, a Polish-backed state.
12 November 1920: the Treaty of Rapallo.
1920: the Guangdong-Guangxi War ends with Guangzhou in the hands of Sun's side.
1920, November: the Whites leave Crimea.
1920, 7-17 November: the Reds break through at Perekop and take the Crimea; Wrangel evacuates 146,000 people, the last boats leaving on 16 November.

1920, 28 October to 3 November: the Red Southern Front's "counteroffensive in northern Taurida between 28 October and 3 November" captured Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol and Chongar; the Perekop-Chongar operation followed on 7-17 November.

1920, 7-17 November: "Between 7 and 17 November it broke through Russian Army defenses on the Isthmus of Perekop" (the Lithuanian Peninsula, the Turkish Wall, Yushun and the Chongar positions), and Wrangel "initiated an evacuation of 146,000 people to Constantinople with the last boats departing on 16 November".
1920, 17 November: the fighting for Northern Taurida and the Crimea ends.
1920, 17 November: the Government of South Russia is dissolved after the loss of the Crimea; South Russia ends.
1920, 28 October to 3 November: the Red Southern Front's "counteroffensive in northern Taurida between 28 October and 3 November" captured Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol and Chongar.
12 November 1920: the Treaty of Rapallo gives Italy Zadar and islands.

1920: Japan receives the League of Nations mandate for the South Seas Islands: 'a League of Nations mandate given to the Empire of Japan by the League of Nations following World War I' (infobox 'Class C League of Nations mandate of Japan (1920-1947)').
3 December 1920: Karabekir 'imposed on Armenia the Treaty of Alexandropol'; Armenia 'was confined to the province of Yerevan, thereby ceding Kars, Nakhchivan, and Surmalu' (page).
2 December 1920: 'due to the threat of a Soviet ultimatum' the government hands power to the Soviets; the Revkom had proclaimed Soviet rule on 29 November.
1920: the occupation ends as the mandate begins.
1920: Australia receives the League of Nations mandate for the Territory of New Guinea, 'German New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago' but not Nauru or German Samoa.
1920, end of the year: Georgia reoccupies the Lori neutral zone.
1920: the Australian military occupation of New Guinea ends as the mandate begins (17 December 1920).

1920: the Japanese occupation of Micronesia gives way to the League of Nations mandate for the South Seas Islands: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands.'
1920: New Guinea passes to Australia.
1920: German Micronesia passes to Japan as the South Seas Mandate: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands.'
1920: German New Guinea ends.
1920: the occupation becomes a mandate: infobox 'League mandate: 17 December 1920'; New Zealand governed the islands 'as a League of Nations Class C Mandate'.
1920: New Zealand receives the Class C mandate over the former German colony (17 December 1920).
1920: German Samoa ends as a state with the mandate.
1920: the occupation of Samoa becomes a mandate.
1920: New Zealand receives the Class C mandate over Western Samoa (Upolu and Savai'i), later a UN trust territory (1946).
1920, 2 December: Soviet Armenia is proclaimed.
24 July 1920: the French invade after the ultimatum of 14 July.
25 July 1920: the fighting ends with the surrender of Damascus to French forces.
25 July 1920: Damascus falls and the kingdom ends.
July 1920: Gouraud attacks Faisal.
24 July 1920: France takes Damascus.
24 July 1920: the French win at Maysaloun 'in less than a day' and Gouraud's forces capture Damascus; the page records no further fighting of the war.

1920, 19 October: Red forces of the FER begin advancing on Chita after the Japanese left it on 15 October; Semyonov had passed his civil powers to a Provisional Eastern-Transbaikal Assembly in September.
1920, 22 October: Chita falls to the Red forces; Semyonov's regime, "left without territory, collapsed" and the FER takes Transbaikal and moves its capital to Chita.
1920, 22 October: fighting for Chita ends with its capture.
1920, October: the capital moves from Verkhneudinsk to Chita ("By October Semenov had been expelled from his base of operations in Chita"; infobox capital Chita from October 1920).

1920: the republic that "was established comprising only the area around Verkhneudinsk" in April is by the 1921 keyframe the whole of Buryatia, Transbaikal and Amur: the page says it "consisted of four provinces ...

1920, 19 October: Red forces of the Far Eastern Republic begin advancing on Chita after the Japanese left it on 15 October; Semyonov passed his civil powers to a Provisional Eastern-Transbaikal Assembly in September.
1920, 22 October: Chita falls to the Red forces; the regime, "left without territory, collapsed" and the Far Eastern Republic takes Transbaikal.
1920, 22 October: fighting for Chita ends with its capture.
1920, 28 October: "Disestablished: October 28" (infobox, no year shown); the page says the regime "left without territory, collapsed" at the end of October.
1920, November: the Maritime Province enters the FER on paper.

the 1919 shape carried into 1920 as the republic's extent at the start of the year; the Turkish invasion of 28 September took the city of Kars on 30 October (ledger loss) and the Treaty of Alexandropol (3 December 1920) confined Armenia 'to the province of Yerevan, thereby ceding Kars, Nakhchivan, a
British Africa without Egypt, occupied Tanzania and the Asian lands and the Union of South Africa; without Libya except the Sarra Triangle

Cliopatria shape of 1920 minus all of Canada except Newfoundland and Labrador, which stay a separate British colony; New Zealand; Kuwait; without the German New Guinea land that Cliopatria adds to the British shape from 1915; without the Indonesian cells of Cliopatria's shape

144,816 km2 for 1920-1921 against the infobox's 127,906 km2 (ratio 1.13): Ruthenia is in, and Cieszyn Silesia is divided at Spa on 28 July 1920 ('58.1% of the area of Cieszyn Silesia, along with 67.9% of the population, was taken over by Czechoslovakia').
the same shape, with the Anatolian part drawn as occupied land (hatched) and Greece, Western and Eastern Thrace as direct land
the 1900 Somali correction and, in Libya, only the five coastal enclaves
the Hejaz with Aqaba and Ma'an, de facto under Hejaz control after Faisal's administration was defeated by the French
299,478 km2, 1920-1931: Trentino-Alto Adige now 51 of 54 cells, Istria, Zara.
60,288 km2: unverified, page budget.

'the German area north of the Memel River' given 'the status of Territoire de Memel' (infobox area 2,657 km2; the Klaipėda Revolt page gives 2,848 km2 including 412 km2 of the Curonian Lagoon); a 30 km radius around Memel (Klaipėda) is the closest name the gazetteer has
1920-1921, 650 thousand km2.

101,646 km2 for 1920-1923, 2,500 km2 below the 1919 shape along the southern border (gazetteer: 10 cells, 24.0-26.5 E, 41.3-41.7 N) for which no page gives a reason (the Treaty of Neuilly page mentions 'a further area of 2,563 km2 on its western border', the same size as the drop but on the western border, not the southern one where the gazetteer finds it, so it is not taken as the cause); kept as
85,624 km2 (-1,589 km2 on 1919): South Tyrol is out; three border cells of Italy remain, which are within the shape's precision.

the Soviet-held land of 1920: Russia proper with the regained Siberia, Don, Kuban, North Caucasus and Crimea, without the Far Eastern Republic (Transbaikal, Amur, the Maritime Province), with the Vitebsk, Mogilev and Gomel governorates
373,273 km2, ratio 0.96 to the infobox's 388,634 km2 (the body gives 389,720 km2 after the Trans-Olza annexation; no year for either).
"the Crimean Peninsula and adjacent areas of the mainland": the former Taurida Governorate, with Northern Taurida (Melitopol, Henichesk) until the Red offensive of 28 October 1920
the 1920 outline and the Asir highlands (Abha) taken in 1920, for 1920 to November 1921
the towns the page lists as the republic's temporary de facto capitals ('Kamianets-Podilskyi; Vinnytsia; Zhmerynka; Proskuriv; Rivne'), each with a 60 km radius
Germany without the Saar, with the occupied Rhineland and, until their loss, Northern Schleswig and East Upper Silesia
the 1920 shape without Zadar, the Italian Province of Zara (the small islands are below the shape's resolution)
1921-1922: the Priamur enclave "was gradually expanded to Khabarovsk and then to Spassk" (the page gives no dates; placed in 1921, between the coup and the October 1922 recapture).
1921: bridge to the 1921 keyframe (Buryatia, Transbaikal and Amur only).
1921: Burgenland passes to Austria.
1921: the enclave grows to Khabarovsk.
1921: the British occupation of the south ends.
1921: the British occupation of the north ends.
1921: Burgenland joins Austria.
1921: Cliopatria's bloc of Soviet republics ends; the four founding republics sign the treaty creating the Soviet Union on 30 December 1922.
1921: the Civil Affairs Bureau, 'initially based in Truk', 'moved to Koror in the Palau islands in 1921'.
1921: Abdulaziz declares himself Sultan of Nejd.
29 January 1921: Hodeidah passes to the Emirate.

1921, 25 February: "On 25 February, after a one-week offence by the Red Army, Tbilisi fell to the Bolsheviks" and the Revolutionary Committee "declared the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic on 25 February 1921".
1921, 11/12 February: the Red Army invades.
February 1921: Ungern-Sternberg takes Urga and restores the Bogd Khan.
1921: Soviet forces withdraw after the Russo-Persian treaty of February 1921, which 'ensured peaceful relations' and resulted in 'the withdrawal of Soviet forces'.
1921: Ungern-Sternberg takes Urga and the Chinese garrison goes.
1921: the Coto War begins.
1921, 25 February: Soviet Georgia is proclaimed.
1921: the Hultschin area goes to Czechoslovakia, 'the transfer was completed on 3 February 1921'.
1921: Belgium hands the Kigoma district to Britain.
1921: Belgium hands Kigoma to Britain.

1921, 18 March: the Treaty of Riga ends the Polish-Soviet War; Poland recognises Soviet Belarus, withdraws from "areas further east, notably Minsk" and keeps western Belarus; the republic left is 52,400 km2 (the BSSR page dates the treaty February 1921).
1921, 17 March: the invasion ends.
1921, March: the Democratic Republic ends and its land becomes the Georgian SSR.

1921, March: the rest of Georgia passes to the Soviet side as the invasion (12 February to 17 March 1921) ends; "In March 1921 the government of the Georgian Democratic Republic was forced into exile" and Batumi is surrendered to the Revkom.

Page silent on whether the Georgian SSR held or administered the Artvin Okrug before the Treaty of Kars; it is drawn from the invasion's end (March 1921) because the page says the republic was "forced to cede the Georgian-dominated Artvin Okrug to Turkey".
18 March 1921: the revolutionaries take Kyakhta Maimaicheng.
February-March 1921: the rest of Outer Mongolia returns to Mongolian rule.
1921: the rest of Outer Mongolia leaves Chinese rule.
1921: the United States stops the Coto War.
1921: Coto passes to Costa Rica.
18 March 1921: the Peace of Riga ends the war.
18 March 1921: Riga leaves Poland Western Belarus and Western Ukraine.
1921 (22 March): Belgium cedes the Kigoma District.
1921, 18 March: the Peace of Riga closes the fighting for the UPR.
1921: the Ukrainian People's Republic ends as a state on Ukrainian soil.

1921, 18 March: the Treaty of Riga ends the Polish-Soviet War; the border runs about 250 km east of the Curzon Line, Poland recognises Soviet Ukraine and Belarus and withdraws recognition from the Ukrainian People's Republic, and western Ukraine goes to Poland.
11 April 1921: the Emirate of Transjordan is established with Abdullah as emir at Amman.
1921, 27 May: a White coup in Vladivostok sets up the Provisional Priamurye Government, 'the last Russian State enclave during the Russian Civil War'.

1921, 23-27 May: a White coup by the Kappelevtsy and the Merkulov brothers takes Vladivostok "to break away from the Far Eastern Republic" (Priamurye page: the government "had its origin in a 1921 White Army coup in Vladivostok and its environs"; infobox predecessor: Far Eastern Republic); the Provisional Priamurye Government is established on 27 May (the Far Eastern Republic page dates the coup 2
1921: the military government becomes an 'extraordinary presidency'.
June 1921: the Rif War begins.
1921: the Kingdom of Iraq is founded under the British mandate.
1921: the Tannu Tuvan People's Republic declares independence.
23 August 1921: the land passes to the kingdom, which Britain then administers.

23 August 1921: the Kingdom of Iraq is founded under the British mandate, which this row carries as an occupation (hatched), as the kingdom-of-iraq dossier does (its British party there is kingdom-of-great-britain).
Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): added.
1921: the Rifians proclaim the Republic of the Rif on 18 September.
1921: the republic is crushed.
1921: the Soviet Republic of Gilan ends in September 1921 and Gilan returns to the Persian government.
1921: the Gilan republic is crushed.
